criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core`: a test builds a temporary git repository with two commits (a CLI command added, an athena.toml section removed, a record schema moving to version 2) and asserts the diff reports exactly those three changes (one added command, one removed config section, one changed record schema) and nothing else, with totals of 3.
criteria.evidence: I ran it: `a_command_added_a_section_removed_and_a_schema_moved_are_exactly_three_changes` passed, along with 6 other design_surface tests. The test makes two commits in a scratch repository with Git::isolated. It compares the whole SurfaceDiff by equality against an expected value that holds only commands.added=[status], config_keys.removed=[budget 'section (2 keys)'] and record_schemas.changed=[athena.candidate], so any extra item would fail it. It also asserts Totals{added:1, removed:1, changed:1, total:3}. One weakness: the schema case goes from versions '1,2' to '2', not from '1' to '2' (see findings).

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test`: a test computes the inventory at this repository's HEAD and asserts it contains every top-level subcommand of the clap Command that `athena --help` prints and every [section] header that the repository's athena.toml uses.
criteria.evidence: I ran it: `the_inventory_at_head_lists_every_command_in_help_and_every_section_athena_toml_uses` passed. It runs the real binary (CARGO_BIN_EXE_athena --help), reads the command names from the Commands: section, and asserts each one is in inventory.commands. It parses athena.toml at HEAD with the toml crate and asserts that every table path is a 'section' in config_keys. For [capabilities.*] it checks only the top level, because that schema is a map. HEAD here is the snapshot's candidate commit. The full suite passed in Athena's CI record.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test`: a test computes the inventory twice at the same commit and asserts the two results are equal and serialize to identical bytes.
criteria.evidence: I ran both tests and both passed: `the_inventory_at_head_is_identical_when_computed_twice` (real HEAD) and `the_inventory_is_identical_when_computed_twice_at_one_commit` (scratch repository). Each asserts the inventory is not empty, that `one == two`, and that serde_json::to_vec(&one) equals serde_json::to_vec(&two). Every kind is a BTreeMap, so the order is fixed.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check`: both are clean; `cargo test` passes as a whole including the records round-trip test that covers the new design-surface AnyRecord variant and check_record_file accepting it.
criteria.evidence: Athena's CI record for 080eae96 shows fmt, clippy and test all passed. I also ran the round-trip test and it passed. It checks the schema string 'athena.design-surface/1', the canonical path records/design-surface/2026-10/<id>.json, that parse(to_json) gives back the same record, that check_record_file accepts it, DesignSurface::latest, and that validate() rejects a short commit and an empty inventory.

findings.summary: Four changed files are not on the expected deliverables list. Each one is needed for the change to build or pass its checks.
findings.evidence: store.rs: Records::load matches over AnyRecord and needs an arm for the new variant (design_surfaces). records/design_surface.rs: a submodule of records.rs, following the existing core/introspection/throughput pattern. The athena-cli test needs CARGO_BIN_EXE_athena to run `athena --help`. shard-timings.txt: xtask/tests/ci_shards.rs requires every test target to be listed. None of them is harmful or unrequested in substance.

findings.summary: The 'schema moves to version 2' fixture goes from versions {1,2} to {2}, which is dropping version 1, not a move from 1 to 2.
findings.evidence: The base RECORDS fixture already has both athena.candidate/1 and /2. The next commit removes /1, so the asserted change is '1,2' -> '2'. The more natural case, athena.role/1 becoming /2 ('1' -> '2'), which docs/records.md uses as its example, has no direct test. diff_kind handles it the same way, so the behavior is right, but the test does not match the request's wording exactly.

findings.summary: The source-text reading is incomplete in ways that would show false surface changes after a refactor: clap `#[command(flatten)]` and tuple variants (`Foo(FooArgs)`) are not followed, attribute parse errors are dropped without notice, and map-valued config sections drop the map-key level.
findings.evidence: A flattened field would be listed as a positional `<name>`. A tuple variant's args are skipped because named_fields returns nothing. `let _ = attr.parse_nested_meta(..)` throws away items after an unparsed one. `capabilities` (BTreeMap<String, CapabilityConfig>) is listed as `capabilities.checks`, not `capabilities.<name>.checks`. main.rs uses none of these clap forms today, so the HEAD inventory is complete now. A more robust option is to walk the clap Command at runtime (e.g. via a tiny helper binary at that commit) or to error on unrecognised forms. The syn approach is reasonable for reading any commit without building it, so this is not a soundness blocker.

summary: The change does what was asked, so the verdict is pass. A new module, athena-core's design_surface.rs, lists Athena's design surface at a given commit: commands and flags, athena.toml sections and keys, record schemas with their versions, roles with their versions, and workspace crates. It reads the files stored in that commit (not the working tree), parses them with syn and toml_edit, and calls no model. A second function compares two of these lists and reports added, removed and changed items for each kind, with totals. A new athena.design-surface/1 record keeps a list for later comparison; it is wired into the record parser, the validity check and Records::load, and has a round-trip test. No CLI command or dependency was added, and config.rs and athena.toml are unchanged. I ran three sets of targeted tests and all passed. In athena-core, 7 tests, including one where two commits differ by an added command, a removed config section and a schema version change, and the comparison reports exactly those three changes, totalling 3. In athena-cli, 2 tests on the repository's own HEAD: one checks every command `athena --help` prints and every section athena.toml uses; the other computes the list twice and gets byte-identical output. In athena-data, the record round-trip test. fmt, clippy and the full test suite passed in Athena's CI record for this commit. CHANGELOG.md and docs/records.md are updated and match the code. I found three minor issues. Four needed files changed that were not on the expected list. The schema test drops version 1 from a schema that had versions 1 and 2, rather than moving a schema from version 1 to 2. And the code that reads the source text skips clap forms that main.rs does not use today (flatten, tuple variants), so a future refactor could show surface changes that did not happen.
